advice: Propose a Strassen candidate that replaces only the n=512 path with one decomposition level and seven calls to the verified dense 256-square NN beta-zero helper. Inside gemm, allocate three reusable dense 256-square FP32 buffers for left operand, right operand, and product. Copy each parent quadrant using its 512-element row stride while forming the seven signed operand sums. For each product, pass a zeroed 22-slot parameter array with [4]=right operand, [10]=left operand, and [16]=dense product; this mapping makes the helper compute row-major left@right. Accumulate each product into the appropriate 512-stride C quadrant using the approved signs: C11 += P1+P4-P5+P7; C12 += P3+P5; C21 += P2+P4; C22 += P1-P2+P3+P6. Zero C before accumulation. Keep allocation, copies, sums, all seven calls, accumulation, and frees inside gemm. On allocation failure and for other sizes, use the unchanged general fallback. The approved equations and signs are algebraically valid; the fewer multiply-accumulate count is not evidence of a speedup. No complete Strassen wrapper has been measured.
risks: The 512-stride quadrants cannot be passed directly to the helper, which requires dense leading dimension 256; copying and recombination traffic may erase arithmetic savings. FP32 operand sums and changed accumulation order increase rounding error, especially for cancellation and scale-separated inputs, so the existing 0.002 tolerance may fail. Validate with existing cases plus deterministic cancellation and scale-sensitive n=512 inputs against a float64 reference computed from the actual FP32 inputs. Check finite output, full overwrite, unchanged inputs, output guards, allocation-failure fallback, general sizes, tails, and n<=0 before timing. Only then collect ten candidate validations with ten alternating paired controls under unchanged settings and gates; report historical and fresh same-mode comparisons separately.
